### Summary

### Summary

When a project depends on several packages that come from **subdirectories of the same Git repository**, `uv sync --frozen` with a **cold cache** intermittently fails:

```text
error: Failed to download and build `pkg-a @ git+https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git@<sha>#subdirectory=pkg-a`
  cause: Git operation failed
  cause: failed to remove directory `<cache>/git-v1/db/<id>`: Directory not empty (os error 39)
```

A Git trace shows one `git init` creating the repository database while a second Git process inspects the same directory and finds it isn't a repository yet. uv then deletes the directory while the first process is still writing into it. A second run, with the database now present, succeeds.

### Environment

- uv 0.12.24
- Git 2.56.0
- GitHub-hosted runner, `ubuntu-26.04` (image 20261025)
- `UV_CACHE_DIR` inside the workspace, not restored from a previous run (cold)
- Git auto-maintenance disabled in the environment (`maintenance.auto=false`, `gc.auto=0`), so this is not #22829

I haven't reproduced it on 0.13.x. I didn't find a related fix in the 0.13.0–0.13.6 release notes.

### Reproduction shape

A project whose lockfile has three dependencies from one repository, pinned to the same commit:

```toml
[project]
dependencies = ["pkg-a", "pkg-b", "pkg-c"]

[tool.uv.sources]
pkg-a = { git = "https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git", tag = "<tag>", subdirectory = "pkg-a" }
pkg-b = { git = "https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git", tag = "<tag>", subdirectory = "pkg-b" }
pkg-c = { git = "https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git", tag = "<tag>", subdirectory = "pkg-c" }
```

Run `uv sync --frozen` from an empty cache, repeatedly.

Results from 20 parallel CI jobs on the same commit:

| Cache | Failed |
| --- | --- |
| Cold (empty `UV_CACHE_DIR`) | 2 of 10 |
| Restored (database for the repository already present) | 0 of 10 |

### Evidence

With `RUST_LOG=uv_git=debug`, uv logs three fetches for the repository, then a single update:

```text
DEBUG Fetching source distribution from Git: https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git
DEBUG Fetching source distribution from Git: https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git
DEBUG Fetching source distribution from Git: https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git
DEBUG Updating Git source `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git`
```

`GIT_TRACE2_EVENT` shows the overlap. Both failing jobs had the same sequence; times are relative to the `git init`:

| Time | Process | Event |
| --- | --- | --- |
| +0 ms | A | `git init`, `def_repo` = `<cache>/git-v1/db/<id>` |
| +14 ms | B | `git rev-parse` starts |
| +14 ms | B | `error`, exits 128: not a repository yet |
| +240 ms | A | killed (signal), after uv aborted |

So a second task inspected the database while the first was still initializing it, treated it as invalid, and removed it.

### What I looked at

In 0.12.24, `GitResolver::fetch` (`crates/uv-git/src/resolver.rs`) takes an exclusive `LockedFile` on `git-v1/locks/<digest of repository URL>` around `GitSource::fetch`. That lock is keyed the same way as the database path, and `LockedFile` uses `flock`, which should exclude a second task in the same process. The trace nonetheless shows a `git rev-parse` against the database running concurrently with `git init`. I didn't find which code path issues that check, so it may run outside this lock, or the lock may not be held across initialization.

### Workaround

Retrying `uv sync` succeeds once the database exists. A warm cache (restored from a previous run) avoids the failure.


### Platform

ubuntu 26.04 amd64

### Version

0.12.24

### Python version

3.14.9
title: Concurrent Git fetches for packages from the same repository race on a cold cache: "failed to remove directory …/git-v1/db/<id>: Directory not empty"
